narration_timeline.text: Why does this red squirrel keep stopping in the middle of its day?
narration_timeline.scene: A real red squirrel perched on a manmade ledge in Berlin; no claim this particular shot is wild woodland.

narration_timeline.text: A tree is both a route through its habitat and a place to pause for food.
narration_timeline.scene: European red squirrel moving or resting on branches in a Ljubljana park.

narration_timeline.text: One red squirrel pauses among the branches while another grips food between its front paws.
narration_timeline.scene: Two separate real red-squirrel videos: squirrel on a branch and a different squirrel visibly eating. Verify the new first shot actually shows the animal; no walnut action or same-animal continuity claimed.

narration_timeline.text: Those small flexible paws help it handle food while it balances on a stump or branch.
narration_timeline.scene: Genuine red squirrel among logs and branches; forepaw function is explanatory narration.

narration_timeline.text: Between meals, the animal moves along branches and checks its surroundings.
narration_timeline.scene: European red squirrel alert among branches; no claim a predator appears.

narration_timeline.text: That is the red squirrel's daily routine: travel through trees, find a safe perch, and eat.
narration_timeline.scene: A genuine red squirrel on a tree trunk, followed by a separate close-up of a red squirrel holding and eating a nut.
